The Court of Settlement found that the respondent failed to establish the where of the original lessee Ghalib Hossain to get rid of the mischief of P.0.16 of 1972 and the alleged possession of the respondent. She also failed to prove that she has been evicted from the case property and with this finding the case was dismissed. Thereafter the respondent moved the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 499 of 1987 challenging the judgment and order passed by the Court of Settlement.

4. It appears that the High Court Division held that the Court of Settlement did not come to nay definite finding as to whether the original owner left the country when President's Order 16 of 1972 came into force and as to whether the absence from Bangladesh is prejudicial to the interest of the country. The High Court Division has held that the Court of Settlement is not competent to set aside a decree passed by the competent civil court. The High Court Division held that the Court of Settlement failed to the real issue i.e. whether the premises in question was an Abandoned Property or not and exceeded its jurisdiction in holding that the civil court decree obtained by the respondent was fraudulent and with this finding the High Court Division made the Rule absolute.

<u>5. Leave was granted to consider the following:-</u>

<u>"It is submitted by Mr. B. Hossain, learned Advocate-on-Record appearing for the petitioner that the onus being on the respondent to show that the property in question is not an abandoned property and the Court of Settlement having come to a definite finding that the respondent failed to discharge that onus, the High Court Division erred in law in holding that the Court of Settlement did not come to any decision as to the abandoned character of the property and further erred in law in shifting the onus of proof upon the petitioner, secondly he submits, the decree for specific performance of contract being a transaction between the vendor and the vendee and not being the kind of decree acceptable to the Court of Settlement for determining the abandoned character of the property, the High Court Division wrongly held that the Court of Settlement neither set aside the decree nor found it to be fraudulent, when in actual fact the Court of Settlement set aside the decree and found it to be fraudulent, Mr. B. Hossain submits that the High Court Division has failed to exercise its jurisdiction on a correct yardstick while interfering with the decision of an inferior court."</u>

6. Learned Additional Attorney General led us through the judgment of the Court of Settlement and of the High Court Division and submits that the High Court Division committed wrong in holding that the Court of Settlement set aside the judgment and decree of a civil court and cancelled the same it is, also submitted that nowhere in the entire judgment the Court of Settlement passed such an order. He submits that the case of the respondent before the High Court Division as well as before the Court of Settlement is that she entered into an agreement with the original lessee Ghalib Hossain and when the lessee failed to execute and register the Kabala a suit for specific performance of contract was filed which was decreed and she obtained a Kabala. Learned Additional Attorney General submits that this obtaining of Kabala is not sufficient to get a favourable order before the Court of Settlement that respondent Shiuli Begum was never dispossessed rather Momtaj Begum was evicted there from for which she also filed another suit for specific performance of contract. So the Court of Settlement clearly found that respondent Shiuli Begum failed to establish that she was in possession of the case property and she also failed to establish the whereabouts of the angina lessee Ghalib Hossein, Respondent also failed to produce the original lease deed of Ghalib Hossain before the Court of Settlement. Learned Additional Attorney General submits that such matters have been set at rest by this Division in the case of C.Q.M.H. Md. Ayub Ali Vs. the 1st Court, of Settlement and Others reported in 47 DLR (AD) 71 wherein it has been held that the decree in the suit for specific performance of contract will show that it has only decided the controversy between the vendor and the vendee and directed the vendor to execute the necessary document in favour of the vendee. Such a decree is not one which is mentioned in proviso (a) to section 5 of P.O. 142 of 1972. It has been held in paragraph 26 of the said decision that it will be seen that in proviso (a) no particular kind of suit has been mentioned. The reference is to any decree or order which has been passed by any court at any time before the publication of the list in the official Gazette. The list shall not include any building if the decree or order is found declaring the building not to be an abandoned property or not to have vested in the Government under the President's order 16 of 1972 or the possession by the Government of the building as an abandoned property under that order to be illegal or invalid or directing the Government or any officer or authority subordinate to it to return, restore of transfer the building to any person. The law has been well settled by this decision of this Division. In the present case before us the decree of specific performance of contract was obtained by the respondent and in this decree no such declaration as aforesaid has been made. The Government may be added as party in such a suit as required under P.O.142 of 1972 but in such a case no relief has been prayed against the Government. The decree does not require the Government to do any-thing.

7. In the present case before us the decree obtained by the respondent is a decree for specific performance of contract and such a decree cannot be a bar to declare a property as Abandoned Property. The respondent failed to prove the whereabouts of the original lessee and also her possession in the case property. From the perusal of the judgment of the Court of Settlement it also appears that the High Court Division was wrong in holding that the Court of Settlement declared the decree null and void. This finding of the High Court Division is wrong in view of the judgment of the Court of Settlement. It is the definite case of the appellant that Momtaj begum was in possession and she was evicted. This respondent Shiuhi Begum was not evicted. Onus lies heavily on the respondent Shiuli Begum to prove that she has been evicted which she failed to discharge. Having considered the judgment of the Court of Settlement and of the High Court Division and after hearing the learned Additional Attorney General for the appellant and the facts and circumstances of the case and in view of the aforesaid decision of this Division and the nature of the case as made out by the respondent before the Court of Settlement and also before the High Court Division we hold that the High Court Division committed wrong and illegality in making the Rule absolute. The High Court Division failed to consider the legal and factual position and came to an incorrect decision which require interfere.

8. The appeal is accordingly allowed. Judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 499 of 1987 is hereby set aside and the Rule earlier issued in this Writ Petition is hereby discharged.

No order as to cost.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave Appeal Nos. 703-704 of 2009
lawyer:
Shamir Kumar Chowdhury alias Kazal Chowdhury and others ------ Respondents ( In C. P No. 704 of 2009)  
Mohammad Ali Akanda, Senior Advocate instructed by Haridas Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners (In both the Cases) 
Mahbubey Alam Senior Advocate instructed by Chowdhury Md. Zahangir, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent No.1. (In C. P. No.703 of 2009) 
Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate instructed by Chowdhury Md. Zahangir, Advocate-on- Record ------ For Respondent No.3 (In C. P No 704 of 2009) 
Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 (In C. P No.703 of 2009) ------ Not represented
Respondent Nos. 1, 2, 4 and 5 (In C. P No.704 of 2009) ------ Not represented
parties:
Rezia Khatun Chowdhurani and others ------ Petitioners (In both the cases)
Vs.
Sayeda Sirajunnessa Khatun and others ------ Respondents (In C.P. No. 703 of 2009)
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated. 17.12.2008 passed by the  High Court Division in Civil Revision Nos.4784 and 4789 of 1995)
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J: Both these Civil Petitions for leave to appeal are directed against the common judgment-passed by the High Court Division disposing of Civil Revision No. 4784 of 1995, and Civil Revision No. 4789 of 1995 analogously and as such both these petitions were heard together and this single judgment will dispose of both the Civil Positions for leave to appeal.

2. The facts necessary for disposal of these civil petitions for leave to appeal, in short, are as follows:-

3. The predecessor of the present petitioner’s late Md. lshaq Ali, as plaintiff instituted. Title Suit No. 31 of 1970 for specific performance of contract against the opposite parties in respect of the suit properties described in schedule to the plaint. The said suit was subsequently transferred to the court of Sub-Judge, Habiganj and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 68 of 1983.

4. The plaintiff’s case, in short, was that the suit property originally belonged to Surendra Chandra Chowdhury who died leaving son Samir Kumar Chowdhury. That Samir Kumar Chowdhury got the suit property as heir of Surendra Chandra Chowdhury and-also as legatee of a will Samir Kumar Chowdhury entered into a contract with the plaintiff on. 30.09.1965 for sale of the suit property at a consideration of Tk. 17,000/-. That it was stipulated in the deed of contract that out of total consideration money Tk. 6,000/- would remain with the plaintiff on account of expenses for arranging a valid employment voucher in the United Kingdom for Samir Kumar Chowdhury and passport, air ticket etc. and that the plaintiff would procure all those within five months from the date of execution of the deed of contract and that the remaining 11,000/- taka would be paid at the time of execution of sale deed after taking necessary income tax clearance etc. That on the date of that agreement possession of the properly was delivered to the plaintiff. That in the meantime the Sub-Divisional Officer, Habigonj issued a notice for acquisition of the suit property under the defence of Pakistan Rules and evicted the plaintiff and the opposite party No. 1 there from. Plaintiff and Samir Kumar Chowdhury then filed Writ Petition No. 99 of 1966 challenging the acquisition of the suit property and got rule which was subsequently made absolute on 09.02.1967. That Samir Kumar Chowdhury also filed Civil Revision No. 851 of 1966 in connection with grant of probate of the will which was ultimately disposed of in favour of Samir Kumar Chowdhury. That the plaintiff ultimately could not procure the employment voucher in U.K. for Samir Kumar Chowdhury as per contract. That Samir Kumar Chowdhury requested the plaintiff to adjust the expenses of the litigations from the said amount of Tk.6,000/- Plaintiff, accordingly, spent Tk. 1,734/- towards the expenses of the writ petition and the civil revision. That the plaintiff subsequently paid Tk. 11,000/- to Samir Kumar Chowdhury by executing a promissory note on 5th Agrahayan 1372 B.S. and the plaintiff was put into possession of a portion of the suit property. That it was agreed upon that the said amount would be adjusted towards the consideration money but, if for any reason the parties decided not to execute the kabala, then Samir Kumar Chowdhury would refund the said amount of Tk. 11,000/- to the plaintiff. That the plaintiff thereafter filed Money Suit No. 10 of 1968 as the limitation of the promissory note was expiring but that suit was dismissed on technical ground. That as the sale deed could not be executed within the stipulated time of five months, Samir Kumar Chowdhury executed a memorandum on 30.07.1966 to the effect that the period of five months as mentioned in the deed of contract would start from the date of disposal of the writ petition and the civil revision. That the defendants Syeda Sirajunnessa Khatun and her husband Abdur Rahman used to live near the suit property and they were aware of the contract between the plaintiff and Samir Kumar Chowdhury and that these two defendants influenced Samir Kumar Chowdhury to issue a notice upon the plaintiff on 15.01.1966 alleging some false and concocted allegations. Thereafter these defendants collusively procured permission from the Deputy Commissioner. Sylhet for sale of the suit property and obtained a sale deed from Samir Kumar Chowdhury in respect of the suit property.

5. Syeda Sirajunnessa Khatun also instituted Title Suit No. 157 of 1977 for declaration of title and recovery of possession against the plaintiff of above mentioned Title Suit No. 68 of 1983 in respect of the same suit land of that suit. This suit was subsequently transferred to the court of Subordinate Judge, Habiganj and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 93 of 1982. The case of Sirajunnessa Khatun was that Samir Kumar Chowdhury proposed to sell the suit property and she agreed and the consideration was fixed at Tk. 5,000/-. That Samir Kumar Chowdhury received 3,000/- taka as earnest money from her and executed a deed of contract dated 23.09.1963 in Anowar of her. That it was stipulated that alter obtaining probate certificate Samir Kumar Chowdhury would execute and register the sub-kabala deed in favour of Syeda Sirajunnessa Khatun. That in 1966 the suit property was acquired and a writ petition was filed challenging that acquisition of the suit property. That in the meantime the plaintiff or Title Suit No. 68 of 1983 trespassed into one room of the suit property. That Samir Kumar Chowdhury told her that the plaintiff obtained a deed of contract on 30.09.1965 on false pretext and assured her to execute the kabala within reasonable time. That after disposal of the writ petition and the civil revision, Samir Kumar Chowdhury executed the kabala deed in favour of Syeda Sirajunnessa Khatun on 15th April, 1968 on taking necessary permission and delivered possession of the suit property except one room where the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 68 of 1983 was in illegal occupation. That Syeda Sirajunnessa Khatun along with Samir Kumar Chowdhury filed a suit for permanent injunction against the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 68 of 1983 and obtained decree. That the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 68 of 1983 had knowledge about the defendant's deed of contract and inspite of that he entered into contract with Samir Kumar Chowdhury on 30.09.1965. That the alleged memo dated 19.10.1965 and 31.07.1966 allegedly executed by Samir Kumar Chowdhury were forged and collusive. That the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 68 of 1983 and his brother Earshad Ali were influential persons and taking advantage of the lawlessness after the liberation of Bangladesh they forcibly entered into the suit property and evicted the tenants and the defendants there from.

6. This suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession filed by Syeda Sirajunnessa Khatun was contested by the plaintiff of the suit for specific performance of contract and the suit for specific performance of contract was contested by Syeda Sirajunnessa Khatun and Samir Kumar Chowdhury. The learned Subordinate Judge disposed of both the suits analogously by the single judgment and order dated 18.09.1986 decreeing the suit for specific performance of contract and dismissing the suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession.

7. Being aggrieved by that judgment and decree Syeda Sirajunnessa Khatun filed Title Appeal No. 26 of 1987 and Title Appeal No. 27 of 1987. The learned Additional District Judge, Habiganj heard both those appeals analogously and by a single judgment and order dated 31.08.1985 allowed the appeals and dismissed the suit for specific performance of contract and decreed the suit for declaration of title and confirmation of possession filed by Syeda Sirajunnessa Khatun. The heirs of plaintiff of the suit for specific performance of contract then filed the above mentioned two revisions and obtained rules. A Single Bench of the High Court Division heard both the rules analogously and by the impugned judgment and order discharged both the rules affirming the judgment and decree of the appellate court below.

8. Being aggrieved by this judgment and order of the High Court Division the petitioners of the civil revisions have filed these two civil petitions for leave to appeal.

<u>9. Mr. Mohammad Ali Akanda, the learned Advocate for the petitioners in both the civil petitions has assailed the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division by making submissions to the effect that the appellate court below fell in error in reversing the judgment and decree of the trial court without examining the evidence on record properly and without assigning any reason for reversing the judgment of the trial court and the learned judge of the High Court Division also affirmed this judgment of the appellate court below mechanically without applying his judicial mind. The learned Advocate has argued that the trial court meticulously examined the evidence adduced by both the parties and came to correct findings and decisions but the High Court Division failed to consider these material evidence relied upon by the trial court; that the High Court Division has failed to appreciate that the trial court on elaborate discussion of evidence and giving reasoning’s came to a just finding, but the appellate court below did not at all consider material evidence and as such came to a wrong finding. The learned Advocate for the petitioners has argued that there has been a gross miscarriage of justice by the impugned judgment of the High Court Division and as such interference of this Division is necessary.</u>

10. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent. Nos.1 and 3 has made submission sup-porting the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division.

11. We have considered the submission of the learned Advocates of both the sides and gone through all the three judgments of the courts below.

<u>12. In this suit the admitted facts were that Samir Kumar Chowdhury was the original owner of the suit property; this Samir Kumar Chowdhury sold the suit property to Syeda Sirajunnessa Khatun by a registered kabala dated 15.04.1968. The case of the plaintiff in the suit for specific performance of contract was that Samir Kumar Chowdhury entered into a contract with him on 23.09.1963 to sell the suit property and during the subsistence of this contract he sold the suit property to defendant Syeda Sirajunnessa Khatun and as such that kabala was not valid. The plaintiff of the suit for specific performance of contract pleaded also that in the contract entered into between him and Samir Kumar Chowdhury there was stipulation to the effect that the plaintiff would procure the employment voucher in U.K. passport, air ticket etc. for Samir Kumar Chowdhury within five months from the date of that contract and if the plaintiff failed to procure those the contract would stand cancelled. But subsequently Samir Kumar Chowdhury extended that period of five months by executing two memoranda and as such the contract remained valid. But it appears that both the appellate court below and the High Court Division on exhaustive analysis of evidence and facts and circumstance on record and on consideration of relevant laws came to the finding that the plaintiffs alleged contract did not exist when Samir Kumar Chowdhury sold the suit land to Syeda Sirajunnessa Khatun in April 1968.  Both the appellate court below and the High Court Division came to a concurrent finding also to the effect that the alleged memoranda allegedly executed by Samir Kumar Chowdhury extending time for procuring the employment voucher etc. for Samir Kumar Chowdhury were forged and were created by the plaintiff.</u>

13. We have examined the evidence on record and considered the facts and circumstances. We find no reason to differ with these concurrent findings of facts arrived at by the appellate court below and, the High Court Division. The High Court Division examined the judgments of the courts below and evidence on record meticulously and finding Ito misreading, non-consideration or misconstruction of evidence by last court of fact upheld the judgment of that court by giving proper reasoning’s. The High Court Division in. its impugned judgment clearly stated that the court of appeal below did not commit any non-consideration, misreading or misinterpretation of evidence on record and did not commit any error of law occasioning failure of justice. We find no reason to interfere with this impugned judgment of the High Court Division.

14. In the circumstances both the civil petitions for leave to appeal be dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 545 of 2006
lawyer:

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 24.1.2006 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3898 of 1997).
full_judgment:
Md. Tafazzul Islam J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 24.1.2006 of the High Court Division passed in Civil Revision No. 3898 of 1997 discharging the Rule.

<u>2. Facts, in brief, are that Mohen Bashi Roy, the predecessor of the petitioners, filed Title Suit No.36 of 1985 in the Court of the then Munsif (now Assistant Judge),  Derai, Sunamganj for declaration of his right, title and interest in the suit land and for further declaration that the experte decree dated 27.5.1985 of the same very Court passed in Title Suit No. 30 of 1985 is illegal, void and not binding upon him on the averments that the suit land belonged to Raj Chandra who died leaving behind three sons namely Mukunda, Bipin and Manindra and after the death of Mukunda and Bipin the entire property devolved up Manindra; in the year 1972 Manindra who was ailing due to his old age brought the plaintiff to his own house and since then the plaintiff had been residing with Manindra; Manindra having died without any issue, the entire property devolved upon Arun Chandra Shil, the heir of Manindra; the plaintiff continued his possession in the suit homestead with the permission of Arun Chandra Shil who on 23.6.1985, at a consideration of Tk.15,000/-, along with other lands, also sold the suit land to the plaintiff by a registered kabala; the defendant No.1 in June 1985 for the first time, claimed the suit land on the basis of a managed exparte judgment and decree dated 27.5.1985 passed in Title Suit No.30 of 1985 in which only the Government was impleaded as a party and further the averments made in the plaint of Title Suit No.30 of 1985 are not correct and that the alleged kabala dated 15.12.1936 as mentioned in the above plaint was an outcome of forgery and the said kabala was never acted upon.</u>

3. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement contending that Jadhunath was the original owner of the suit land and Raj Chandra, who was his under raiyat, took a loan of Tk. 172 / -from Jadhunath and being unable to the pay that loan Raj Chandra, by kabala dated 15.12.1936, sold the suit land along with other land to Jadhunath and after the above transfer Raj Chandra, having no other land of his own for his living, started living in the suit land with his family members with the permission of Jadhunath and after the death of Raj Chandra, his three sons Mukunda, Bipin and Manindra, with the permission of Jadhunath, resided therein; Jadhunath having died leaving his son Jogesh Chandra the father of the defendant No.1 and then Mukunda, Bipin and Manindra with the permission of Jogesh Chandra, resided therein; Mukunda, Bipin and Manindra and Mukunda having died without leaving any issue, Jogesh Chandra transferred the suit land to the defendant No. 1 by a registered will on the basis of which he owned and possessed the suit land and since he had been possessing the suit land physically, the preparation of the S.A. record in the name of Bipin and others was wrong; the defendant No.1 after coming to know about the wrong recording of S.A. record, filed Title Suit No.30 of 1985 in Falgun 1391 which was decreed on 25.5.1985. The plaintiff having requested the defendant No.1 to accommodate him in the suit premises for same period, he out of sympathy, allowed the plaintiff to stay in the suit premises and the alleged deed on the basis of which the plaintiff claimed title is fraudulent and the plaintiff had not title in the suit land.

4. The learned Assistant Judge, after hearing, decreed the suit. Being aggrieved the defendant No.1 preferred Title Appeal No. 43 of 1986 and the learned Additional District Judge Sunamganj, after hearing, by judgment and decree dated 6.8.1997 allowed the appeal and thereby dismissed the suit. On revision the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3839 of 1987, after hearing, discharged the Rule.

5. We have heard the learned advocate-on-record for the petitioner and perused the impugned judgment and order and the connected papers.

<u>6. As it appears the High Court Division found that Mohan Bashi Roy, the plaintiff, without filing the kabala deed dated 23.6.1985 allegedly executed by Arun Chandra Shill in his favour which is the basic document of his title, merely submitted a certified copy of the same and also took no steps to prove the transfer of title  The Lawyers in his favour and the records of the appellate Court did not show that the original kabala deed dated 23.6.1985 was ever submitted before the learned Additional District Judge nor any prayer was made by the plaintiff to enable him to prove the fact of said transfer; further the trial Court decreed the suit assuming that the plaintiff having proved his possession in the suit land for more than the statutory period of limitation acquired title by adverse possession although the plaintiff, in the plaint, did not seek declaration of title in the suit land on the basis of adverse possession; moreover the plaintiff, who examined him as P.W. 1, in his cross-examination admitted that he started to reside in the suit homestead as a licensee under Manindra; further the plaintiff had set up his claim of possession firstly as a licensee under Manindra and thereafter on the strength of the kabala deed dated 23.6.1985 executed by Arun Chandra Shil in his favour, the subsequent claim of the plaintiff on the basis of kabala dated 23.6.1986 has no basis at all because admittedly the suit land is situated within the territorial jurisdiction of Derai Sub-registry Office but the plaintiffs kabala dated 23.06.86 allegedly executed by Arun Chandra Shil was registered at the Sunamganj Sub-registry Office on including fictitious land only to attract the jurisdiction of Sunamganj Sub-registry Office and further the plaintiff had failed to produce any document at the trial to show that the land included in the kabala belonged to Arun Chandra Shil nor any evidence is available on recorded to show that the said land belonged to Arun Chandra Shil; in view of the above the kabala dated 23.06.85, if any, being registered offending the provision of section 28 of the Registration Act is nothing but a void deed. Further in the case of Abdus Samad Mohammad vs. Deputy Commissioner and Custodian of Vested Property and others reported in 52 PRESENT DLR (AD) 121 it has been held that possession for more than the statutory period of limitation as a licensee does not create any title.</u>

7. We are of the view that the High Court Division on proper consideration of the materials on record arrived at a correct decision. The learned counsel could not point at any illegality or infirmity in the decision of the High Court Division so as to call for any interference.

8. The petition is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 2512-2514 of 2009
lawyer:

parties:

Hajee Abdul Majid ------ Petitioner (in C. P. Nos. 2513-2514 of 2009) 
Vs.
Abdul Mannan and others ------ Respondents (In C. P. No. 2512 & 2514 of 2009)
Jahir Uddin and others ------ Respondents (In C. P. No. 2513 of 2009)
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 19.07.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision Nos.1499 of 2004, 2316 of 2007 and 2047 of 2007)
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J.: All these three Civil Petitions for leave to appeal have been directed against the judgment and order dated 19.07.2009 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division disposing of three Civil Revision Nos. 1499 of 2004, 2316 of 2007 and 2047 of 2007 analogously

2. The relevant facts necessary for disposal of these civil petitions for leave to appeal, in short, are as follows:-

3. One Hajee Abdul Majid filed Other Class Suit No. 113 of 1995 against the Deputy Commissioner, Mymensingh and some other persons for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in 2.85 acres of land out of total 35.35 acres of land of C.S. Plot. No.102 of C.S. Khatian Nos. 3, 13, 14 and 15 of mouza Rabirmara, Fulpur, District-Mymensingh. The case of this plaintiff, in short, was that this land originally belonged to Charu Chandra, Gopal Dhar Chowdhury, Raja Shashi Kanta Acharjee, Satindra Kumar Chowdhury and others. That since the Plaintiff had his own land in plot Nos. 37, 39 and 41 to the contiguous north of this suit land of plot No.102 the plaintiff, since his predecessors' time, had been possessing the suit land for more than 90 years. That though the plaintiff thus acquired good title in this suit land by virtue of adverse possession the suit land was wrongly recorded in the khas khatian of the government and taking advantage of this wrong recording of the suit land the defendant No. 12 and many others took settlement of the suit land from the government illegally.

4. The defendants, in different sets contested that suit. Their material case was that the suit land, admittedly, was the khas land of the original Jamindars and as such, after acquisition of Jamindars, the suit land vested in the government and as such has been rightly recorded in the khas khatian of the government. That the plaintiff has no right, title and possession in the suit land. That the suit land has been rightly and legally, leased out to different persons by the government.

<u>5. The trial court, on consideration of the evidence adduced by all the contesting parties, and the facts and circumstances dismissed that Other Class Suit No.113 of 1995 by the judgment and order dated 27.01.1999. Against that judgment and decree of the trial court the plaintiff preferred Other Class Appeal. No. 55 of 1999 and the appellate court allowed the appeal on contest against the defendant Nos. 1 to 4 and defendant Nos. 8 to 12 by the judgment and order dated 01.03.2007 and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court and decreed the suit declaring the plaintiffs title in the suit land and also confirming the plaintiffs possession therein.</u>

6. Being aggrieved by the judgment and order of the appellate court below the defendant Nos. 8 to 11 filed Civil Revision No. 2316 of 2007 and some other defendants filed Civil Revision No. 2047 of 2007.

7. Claiming the selfsame land of plot No. 102 Mr. Abdul Mannaf and his three brothers filed Title Suit No. 120 of 1997 against the government, Md. Hanif Uddin, Abdul Majid ((he plaintiff of earlier Other Class Suit No. 113 of 1995) and Md. Najim Uddin. In that suit the plaintiffs claimed for declaration of their title in 1.50 acres of land of plot No. 102 of mouza Rabirmara, District-Mymensingh and also for a further declaration that the cancellation of the lease of this land in favour of the defendant No. 7 was collusive, wrong, without jurisdiction etc.

8. The plaintiffs' case, in short, was that the suit land belonged to the government and that the defendant No. 7 Md. Najim Uddin took settlement of the suit land from the government on 25.10.1978 in Settlement Case No. 117 (XIII) 78-79 by registered kabuliat. That Md. Najim Uddin after taking settlement of that land possessed the same for long 15/16 years and thereafter on 22.01.1995 he sold the suit land to the plaintiffs by a registered kabala dated 22.01.1995 and since then the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land. That the defendant No. 6 Abdul Majid though filed Other Class Suit No. 113 of 1995 claiming title in the suit land by virtue of adverse possession but that suit was dismissed on contest. That the cancellation of settlement of the suit land in favour of Md. Najim Uddin has cast cloud in the title of the plaintiff and hence the suit.

<u>9. In. that suit the defendant Nos.1 to 4 and defendant Nos. 5 and 6 contested. The case of the defendant Nos. 1 to 4 governments was that the defendant No. 7 took settlement of the suit land from the government collusively and fraudulently and as such the government subsequently cancelled that settlement lawfully and legally. That the defendant No. 7 never possessed the suit land and the plaintiffs also never possessed the suit land.</u>

10. The case of the defendant Nos. 5 and 6 (the plaintiff of earlier suit No. 113 of 1995) was that they from their predecessors time, had been possessing the suit land with his other contiguous land for more than 90 years and thus they acquired title in the suit land by virtue of adverse possession.

11. The trial court decreed that Other Class Suit No. 120 of 1997 by the judgment and order dated 30.11.1999. Against that judgment and order of the trial court the contesting defendant Nos.5 and 6 preferred Other Class Appeal No. 22 of 2000. The appellate court below, by the judgment and order dated 19.02.2004, allowed that appeal setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial court.

12. Being aggrieved by that judgment and decree of the appellate court below the plaintiff-respondents filed Civil Revision No. 1499 of 2004.

13. Since all these above three civil revisions relates to the same property and the contesting, parties also are same, the High Court Division heard all the three revisions together and disposed of them by the impugned analogous judgment and order dated 19.07.2009. The High Court Division made the rules issued in all those three civil revisions absolute and consequently set aside the judgment and decree of the appellate court below passed in Other Appeal No. 55 of 1999 and Other Appeal No. 22 of 2000.

14. Being aggrieved by this judgment and order of the High Court Division Hajee Abdul Majid, the plaintiff of Other Class Suit No. 113 of 1995 has filed the Civil Petition for leave to appeal Nos. 2513 and 2514 of 2009 and Md. Hanifuddin and Hajee Abdul Majid have filed the Civil Petition for leave to appeal No. 2512 of 2009.

15. We have heard Mr. Abdul Baset Majumder, the learned Counsel for the petitioners in all the above three Civil Petitions For leave to appeal and Mrs. Sufia Khatun, the learned advocate-on-record for the respondent Nos. 1 to 4 in all these three Civil Petitions for leave to appeal.

16. Mr. Abdul Baset Majumder, the learned Counsel has made submissions to the effect that these petitioners have proved their exclusive possession in the suit land by adducing sufficient evidence and that the lower appellate court the last court of fact considering these. evidence and other facts and circumstances rightly found these petitioners' possession and also title by adverse possession in the suit land, but the High Court Division without considering this finding of the last court of fact disbelieved these petitioners possession and title in the suit land without assigning any cogent reason; that the specific case of these petitioners was that they acquired title in the suit land by virtue of long adverse possession since 1910, i.e. more than 60 years and the court of fact, i.e. the appellate court also, on consideration, of evidence on record found this claim of these petitioners proved, but the High Court. Division discarded these findings and decision of the appellate court below on the ground that these petitioners never paid rent to the government. The learned Counsel for the petitioners has argued that this observation of the High Court Division is palpably wrong inasmuch as these petitioners claimed title in the suit land by virtue of adverse possession and as such the question of payment of rent did not arise at all; that the appellate court. below correctly held that these petitioners acquired title over 2.85 acres of land by virtue of adverse possession, but without reversing this finding of the final court of facts the High Court Division made the rule absolute committing gross error of both facts and law. Mr. Abdul Baset Majumder, the learned Counsel has argued also that the settlement of the suit land in favour of some defendants of Other Class Suit No.120 of 1997 was cancelled by the appropriate authority in accordance with law and the High Court Division without giving any findings as to that 'cancellation of the settlement of the suit land has made the rule absolute which has been illegal and has caused serious miscarriage of justice.

17. Mrs. Sufia Khatun, the learned advocate for the respondent Nos. 1-4 has made submissions supporting the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. .

18. We have considered the submissions of the learned advocates of both the sides and gone through the judgments of all the courts below and other materials on record.

19. We find substance in the submissions of the learned Counsel for the petitioners.

<u>20. So leave is granted in all the three civil petitions on ground Nos. 1 and 2 which are quoted below:-</u>

<u>"I. Because the defendant-petitioners proved their exclusive and adverse possession by adducing evidence and the lower appellate court considering this aspect dismissed the suit but the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division without considering  this aspect made the Rule absolute and thereby committed an error which caused serious miscarriage of justice."</u>

<u>II. Because the specific case of the defendant-petitioners is of adverse possession. They claimed title over the suit land as they are possession the suit land adversely since 1910 i.e. more than 60 years but the Single Judge of the High Court Division made the Rule absolute on the ground that the opposite parties (present petitioners) never paid rents to the Government where the case is for adverse possession making the Rule absolute on the ground of non-payment of rent is an error of law which caused failure of justice."</u>

21. Security of Tk. 1,000/- for each case is to be deposited within 1(one) month.

22. The petitioner’s are permitted to prepare the paper book out of Court in accordance with Rules.

23. The parties are directed to maintain status-quo in respect of the suit land till disposal of the appeals.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 16th January, 2005 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 9779 of 1991)
full_judgment:
Md. Tafazzul Islam J : This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the : judgment dated 16.1.2005 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 9779 of 1991, discharging the Rule obtained against the judgment and decree dated 19.2.1986 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge). Moulvibazar in Title Appeal No. 2 of 1985 affirming those of dated 25th November, 1984 passed by the Teamed Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Kulaura, Moulvibazar in Title suit No. 66 of 1983 dismissed the suit.

2. The predecessor of the petitioners namely Sonawer Ali, as plaintiff, filed the above suit (previously Title Suit No. 221 of 1978) seeking declaration of his title in the suit land on the averments, inter alia, that the suit land measuring 1.00 acre, originally belonged to Pyari Charan Debnath who died leaving behind son, kunja Debnath, widow, Tarangini Bala; Kunja Debnath sold the suit land to the plaintiff by registered kabala dated 22.10.1956 and Tarangini Bala also executed a deed of relinquishment in his favour on 10th June, 1958 acknowledging the above transfer to the plaintiff by kabala dated 22.10.1956 and since then the plaintiff has been possessing the same exclusively and thereafter the defendant Nos. 1-4 having dispossessed him from the suit land the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 194 of 1958 in the Court of 2nd Munsif, Moulvibazar against them for declaration of title and for recovery of possession which was decreed on contest and the above defendant Nos. 1-4 then preferred Title Appeal No. 208 of 1959 but the lower appellate court, after hearing, also affirmed said decree and the defendant Nos. 1-4 then preferred Second Appeal No. 259 of 1960, before the High Court Division which after hearing was dismissed; in pursuance of the said decree the plaintiff filed Title Execution Case No. 11 of 1965 and in the above execution proceeding the plaintiff got khas possession of the suit land through court; thereafter while in peaceful possession of the suit land the plaintiff, on 27th July 1978, came to know that the suit land has been wrongly recorded jointly in his name as well as in the names of the defendants even though the defendants have no right, title, interest or possession in the suit land and as the wrong recording of the suit land clouded his title in the suit land, hence the suit.

3. The defendant No. 5, the predecessor of respondent Nos. 1-6 herein, contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all material allegations made in the plaint and contending that the plaintiff, who is his brother, is a literate man while the defendant No.5 is an illiterate man and that the plaintiff had no other separate source of income except the joint family property and that the defendant No.5 purchased the suit land jointly with the plaintiff with the joint income and that the defendant No.5 and the plaintiff were also in joint mess and possessed the suit land jointly and accordingly the suit land has been recorded in their names jointly; there was an amicable partition of the joint properties of the defendant No. 5 and the plaintiff in the year 1968 the suit land feel in the share of the defendant No. 5; on receiving the summons of the suit the defendant No.5, for the first time, came to know about the alleged kabalas in favour of the plaintiff alone. The trial court, after hearing, dismissed the suit. As against that the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No.2 of 1985 and after hearing, the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Moulvibazar, dismissed the appeal. Then the plaintiff moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 63 of 1968 (Sylhet), which subsequently renumbered as Civil Revision No. 9779 of 1991 (Dhaka).

<u>4. As it appears both the trial court as well as the lower appellate court disbelieved the case of the plaintiff that he purchased the suit land from his personal income which he earned after getting the license; of export and import in the year 1966; the trial court specially found it incredible that the plaintiff, within such a short time of starting his probate business, could purchase the suit land and observed that the plaintiff failed to prove his business from which he obtained money to purchase the suit land and accordingly dismissed the suit holding that the fact of previous separation of the brothers prior to purchase of the suit land could not be presumed to be true and the plaintiff failed to prove separate business and the claim of purchase of the suit land out of his own earning and the plaintiff also failed to prove his exclusive title in the suit land, the lower appellate court further found that the plaintiff did not file any document for proving that he got the possession of the suit land after evicting the defendants of earlier suit i.e. Title Suit No. 208 of 1959 and the lower appellate court also observed that P.W.2 gave a confusing statement regarding the identity of the suit land and the separation of both the brothers and the plaintiff also could not prove that he purchased the suit land out of his exclusive fund and further since the plaintiff did not relay the suit land with the land mentioned in the suit kabala, his claim in the suit land has not been proved. As it appears in view of the above the High Court Division discharged the Rule holding that in revisional jurisdiction the Court is not competent to interfere with the finding of facts arrived at by the lower appellate court, the final court of facts, and so in view of the above concurrent findings of the courts below, which are based on materials on record and on evidence and also in the absence of error of law or procedure affecting merit of the case, cannot be disturbed and that the plaintiff has failed to prove that he purchase the suit property out of his own income and that the court of appeal below on assessing the oral evidence on record afresh also could not find anything to believe the case of the plaintiff.</u>

5. We have heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and also perused both the judgments and the materials on record.

6. We are of the view that after due consideration of evidence, both oral and documentary and the other attending circumstances both the trail court as well as the lower appellate court came to a concurrent finding and accordingly in the absence of any instance of misreading of evidence or non consideration of the materials on record the High Court Division, in revisional jurisdiction, did not interfere with the said decision and there is also no error or impropriety in the decision of the High Court Division which calls for any interference by this Division and further no point of law is also involved in this leave petition.

7. The petition is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2298 of 2009
lawyer:
Mohammad Ali Akanda, Advocate instructed by Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners 
Md. Asaduzzaman, Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent Nos.1-3, 10 & 12

Hozizur Rahman and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Abu Bakar Chowdhury and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 19.05.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4014 of 2008)
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J.: This civil petition has been filed seeking leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 19.05.2009 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4014 of 2008.

2. The relevant facts necessary for disposal of this civil petition for leave to appeal, in short, are as follows:-

3. On 22.11.1993 the present Plaintiff-respondents filed Title Suit No. 66 of 1993 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Habigonj for declaration of their title in the suit land and for further declaration that the auction sale of the suit land did not affect the plaintiff’s title in the said land. That Title Suit was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 213 of 1994.

4. The present defendant-petitioners appeared in that suit and filed an application praying for rejection of the plaint stating that according to the plaint case itself the plaintiffs earlier filed a title suit being. Title Suit No. 159 of 1966 in respect of the same suit land and that suit was dismissed and as such the present suit was not maintainable.

<u>5. The plaintiffs contested the said application for rejection of the plaint by filing written objection contending that the subject matter, parties and the relief sought for in the said Title Suit No. 156 of 1966 and those of the present suit were not same; that the application for rejection of plaint was misconceived and so the same should be rejected.</u>

6. The learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Habigonj by his order No. 145 dated 26.10.2005 rejected the said application for rejection of the plaint but stayed further proceedings of Title Suit No. 213 of 1994 till final adjudication of Title Suit No. 159 of 1966. Against the said order the plaintiff filed Civil Revision No. 14 of 2006 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Habigonj which was ultimately heard by the learned Additional District Judge, Habigonj, who by the order dated 07.10.2008, disallowed the said revision affirming the order of the learned Joint District Judge. Against that order of the Additional District Judge, Habigonj the plaintiffs filed above mentioned Civil Revision No. 4014 of 2008 and obtained rule which was ultimately disposed of by a Single Bench of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order,

7. The High Court Division, upon hearing both the parties and considering the relevant papers found out that the earlier Title Suit No.  159 of 1966 was dismissed by the judgment and order dated 15.09.1970 against which Title Appeal No.  38 of 1971 Was filed and the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet disposed of that appeal sending hack the suit for retrial and against that judgment of the 1st appellate court Second Appeal No. 18 of 1973 was filed before the High Court Division and by the judgment and order dated 27.07.1979 the High Court Division sent back the case to the appellate court below with a direction to dispose of the appeal on merit, but after receipt of the records by the lower appellate court the records of both the Title Appeal No. 38 of 1971 and the connected Title Suit No. 159 of 1966 got missing. Upon finding out the above facts and considering the circumstances the High Court Division disposed of the rule giving direction to the learned District Judge, Habigonj to take effective steps to reconstruct the case records of Title Suit No. 1 59 of 1966 and Title Appeal No. 38 of 1971 and direction to the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Habigonj also to reconsider the order of stay on perusal of papers of Title Suit No. 159 of 1966 and Title Appeal No. 38 of 1971 after their reconstruction and also to dispose of the Title Appeal No. 38 of 1971 expeditiously after reconstruction. In this impugned judgment and order the High Court Division made directives also to the effect that till reconstruction of the records of Title Suit No. 159 of 1966 and Title Appeal No. 38 of 1971 the order of stay granted on 26.10.2005 by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Habigonj will remain in force and the same shall stand vacated if those records are not reconstructed within 6 (six) months from the date of receipt of that order and the trial of Title Suit No. 213 of 1994 shall proceed.

8. Mr. Mohammad Ali Akanda, the learned Advocate for the petitioners has assailed this very last part of the impugned order directing for reconstruction of the records within 6 months from the date of receipt of the order, in default, for proceeding with the trial of the Title Suit No. 213 of 1994. The learned Advocate has argued that the High Court Division has erred in law in giving this very direction ignoring the provision of Section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate has contended that this direction for proceeding with the trial of the Title Suit No. 213 of 1994 after 6 months even if the records of earlier suit is not reconstructed within this time-has been in violation of Section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure and as such it is illegal.

9. Mr. Md. Asaduzzaman, the learned Advocate for the respondents has made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order.

<u>10. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides and the facts and circumstances. We find no illegality or impropriety in the impugned order of the High Court Division. In the stated facts and circumstances the High Court Division rightly fixed a time limit for reconstruction of the records of earlier Title Suit No. 159 of 1966 and Title Appeal No. 38 of 1971. An indefinite period cannot be allowed for reconstruction of these records. 6 months time is sufficient for reconstruction of these records in the circumstances where both the parties of these suits are present before the court. It should be mentioned here that in the impugned order the High Court Division has given direction to both these parties also to assist the court for reconstruction of these records. Where both the parties have come again before the court in a subsequent suit admitting that there was an earlier suit in respect of the same property both these parties have responsibilities to produce necessary materials, papers, particulars etc to the court for the purpose of reconstruction of those records and if the parties supply these necessary materials before the Court then there will be no difficulty to reconstruct the records within the time fixed by the High Court Division.</u>

<u>11. However, the subsequent suit cannot he kept stayed for an indefinite period. In the circumstances where there is no proof before the court to prove that actually the earlier suit was in between the same parties or their representatives in respect of the same property  and the issues to be decided in both the suits are also same the subsequent suit should not be kept stayed for an indefinite period.</u>

12. So, we find nothing to interfere with-the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division which has been most proper and justified in the given facts and circumstances. This civil petition for leave to appeal is, therefore, dismissed.

End.

case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated March 9, 2006 passed by the High Court Division in 2631 of 1996)
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin CJ: This petition for leave to appeal has been filed against the judgment and order dated March 9, 2006 of a single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2631 of 1996 making the Rule absolute upon setting aside the judgment and decree dated April 18, 1996 of the Court of Additional District Judge, Madaripur in Title Appeal No. 38 of 1995 allowing the appeal and thereby decreeing the suit upon setting aside the judgment and decree dated March 28, 1995 of the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Razior, Madaripur in Title Suit No. 26 of 1992 dismissing the same.

<u>2. The suit was filed seeking declaration that the preliminary decree dated July 18, 1988 and the final decree dated August 30, 1989 passed in Title Suit No. 42 of 1986 and the possession of the partitioned land obtained through the Title Execution Case No. 10 of 1989 are illegal, void, Collusive, null and void, fraudulent, inoperative, without jurisdiction, malafide and not binding upon the plaintiffs.</u>

3. Title Suit No. 26 of 1992 was filed averring, that the land in suit was recorded in the R.S. Khatian in the name of Makim Bepari and others, that by a partition deed dated August 13, 1948 the land of A.S. khatian was partitioned among the co-sharers, that Makim Bepari while owning and possessing the land in suit died leaving   his brother Munsur Bepari as the sole heir, that the plaintiffs purchased the land in suit and the other land on October 30, 1973, that plaintiffs in connection with their service were staying at different places and because of that they entrusted management of the land to Majid Mia, that the defendant Nos. 1-27 to grab the land in suit filed Title Suit No. 42 of 1986, that inspite of non-service of summons Mazid Mia informed plaintiff No.1 about the filing   of the suit and he entrusted Mazid Mia for taking steps in the suit, that Mazid Mia being gained over by the defendant Nos.1-27   did not take steps in the suit and that finally defendant Nos. 1-27 upon practicing fraud on the Court obtained ex-parte decree on July 18, 1988 in preliminary form and the said decree was made final on August 30, 1989 and that on the basis of the fraudulent decree the defendant Nos. 1-27 started Title Execution Case No.10 of 1989 and no notice of Title execution case was served on the plaintiffs, that plaintiffs entrusted management of the land in suit to Majid Mia and that the plaintiffs upon making construction let out the premises in suit to different tenants, that in 1992 plaintiff No.1 after retiring from the service went to his village home and thereafter went to the Court for ascertaining position of the suit and from an information slip obtained through the clerk of an Advocate, the plaintiff No. 1 came to know about the decree dated July 18, 1988 and August 30, 1989 and that also delivery of possession of the partitioned land in pursuant to the order passed in Title Execution Case No.10 of 1989.

4. The suit was contested by the defendant Nos. 1, 2, 4-6 and 8-12 by filing written statement denying the averments made in the plaint and stating, inter alia, that the land in suit was never owned and possessed by Makim Bepari alone, that R.S. record was wrongly prepared in the name of Shafiz Uddin Bepari and others, that Shafiz Uddin Bepari and others possessed 15½ decimals of land, that Taleb Ali Bepari and Gaizuddin Bepari had equal share in the land in suit, that there were Mosque, Madrasha and Charitable dispensary in the land in suit and the said institutions were shifted to some other place and thereupon the two co-sharers divided the land equally among them, that Gaiz Uddin died leaving two Sons - Shofizuddin and Kafiluddin and one daughter Asia, that the plaintiffs are the heirs of the Shofizuddin and Kafiluddin, that the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 upon claiming the land in suit on the basis of purchase on Chaitra 6, 1392 B.S. while asked the defendants to remove the structures then they filed the Suit No. 42 of 1986.

5. It was the definite case of the contesting defendants that the summons were duly served upon the defendants of the Title Suit No.42 of 1986.

6. The trial Court dismissed the suit on the finding that the plaintiffs failed to prove their case i.e. non-service of summons of the Title Suit No. 42 of 1986 and also did not accept the case of the plaintiffs that plaintiff No.1 came to know about the decree passed in Title Suit No. 42 of 1986 on the basis of information slip claimed to have obtained through the clerk of an Advocate.

7. As against the aforesaid judgment and decree the plaintiffs went an appeal. The appellate Court allowed the appeal primarily on the finding since plaintiffs and defendants are co-sharers in the land in suit ought the Title Suit No, 42 of 1986 to not have been decreed ex-parte. The appellate Court also observed that notice of the title execution case was not served upon the plaintiffs who were defendants in Title Suit No. 42 of 1986. The appellate Court declared the decree passed in Title Suit No.42 of 1986 and also the proceeding of the Title Execution Case No. 10 of 1989 illegal. The contesting defendants moved the High Court Division as against the judgment and decree of the appellate Court in revisional jurisdiction and obtained Rule.

8. It is seen from the judgment of the appellate Court that the Said Court disposed of the appeal without discussing the evidence although trial Court on discussion of the evidence of the parties arrived at the finding that summons of the Title Suit No. 42 of 1986 was served on the defendants of the said suit and that knowledge about the decree passed in Title Suit No. 42 of 1986 upon obtaining information slip through the clerk of an Advocate was not established and consequently the suit so filed was barred by limitation.

9. The High Court Division in the back-ground of the materials on record held that the summons of Title Suit No. 42 of 1986 was duly served on the plaintiffs of the instant suit and they contested the suit by engaging lawyer.

10. It may be mentioned that the trial Court dismissed the suit on the ground of maintainability since the possession through Title Execution Case No. 10 of 1989 was delivered to the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 42 of 1986 and as such in the absence of seeking consequential relief i.e. recovery of possession the suit was not maintainable. The appellate Court did not address itself to the said vital aspect of the case and the question of law. The High Court Division as seen from the judgment sought to be appealed considered the question of limitation as well as maintainability of the suit and thereupon set aside the judgment of the appellate Court.

11. We have heard the learned Advocate-on-Record and perused the materials on record.

<u>12. The trial Court dismissed the suit on the definite finding that the summons of the Title Suit No. 42 of 1986 was served upon the plaintiffs i.e. defendants of the said suit and they contested the suit and that the Title Suit No.26 of 1992 was barred by limitation since the same was filed beyond 3 years from the date of passing of the decree and that knowledge about the decree as asserted in the plaint could not be established by the plaintiffs. The trial Court also considered the question of maintainability of the suit in the background of absence of non-service of consequential relief, i.e. recovery of possession which was obtained by the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 42 of 1986 upon putting   the decree obtained in Title Suit No. 42 of 1986 into execution by filing Title Execution Case No. 10 of 1989. The appellate Court as seen from the judgment of the said Court did not avert at all to the aforesaid findings of the trial Court Nor did consider the evidence of the parties. The appellate Court being the last Court of fact and while reversing the judgment of the trial Court was required to interfere with the judgment of the trial Court upon reversing the findings of the trial Court on due consideration of the evidence, but the appellate Court did not do so. The High Court Division in our view has not committed any error in setting aside the judgment of the appellate Court and thereupon, restoring the judgment of the trial Court. The learned Advocate-on-Record could not point out error of the kind in the judgment of the High Court Division calling for interference by this Division.</u>

13. In the background of the discussion made hereinabove we find no merit in the petition.

14. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed

End.

case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated 16.7.91 passed by the High Court Division in Appeal from Original Decree No 22 of 1981)
full_judgment:
A. M. Mahmudur Rahman J:- This appeal by leave at the instance of defendant No. 1 appellant is against the judgment and order dated 16.7.91 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 22 of 1981 allowing the appeal on setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the teamed Subordinate Judge, First Court Mymensingh in O.C. Suit No.102 of 1973.

2. The plaintiff the people's Republic of Bangladesh respondent instituted O.C. Suit No. 102 of 1973 against defendant No.1, Md. Shamsul Huda and defendant No. 2 Benode Lal Roy for declaration that the ex-parte decree passed in O.C. Suit No. 35 of 1969 for specific performance of contract and the deed of transfer obtained on the basis of the said decree are illegal null and void on the averments, inter alia that the suit property belonged to one Lala Ram Sankar who died unmarried and sarna Kumari was a maid servant of Lala Ram. After the death of Lala Ram she used to look after his properties through her servant defendant No. 2 Ronade Lal Roy. On her death defendant No.2 in collusion with defendant No.1 created a fraudulent and ante-dated bainapatra purported to have been executed by Sarna Kumari on 17.12.63 and after the death of Sarna Kumari defendant No.1 filed O.C. suit No.35 of 1969 for specific performance of contract for the suit property showing defendant No.2 as heir of Sarna Kumari and on the basis of the said bainapatra got an ex-parte decree. The plaintiff was in possession of the suit properties through tenants and title of the plaintiff Government to the property in Suit was clouded by the said decree and the sale deed. Hence the suit.

3. Defendant No.1 contested the suit. His of case was that the suit properties are self-acquired properties of Sarna Kumari Roy and she was in possession therein for more than 12 years. She entered into a contract on 17.12.63 for sale of the property in suit for Tk. 39,000/- with defendant No.1 and on receipt Tk. 38,100/- She delivered possession of a portion; of the property to him. If was stipulated in the bainapatra that Sarna Kumari would take clearance from Income Tax Authority for transferring the property. In the meantime she died leaving behind defendant No. 2, her mother's sister's son as a sole heir. On refusal of defendant No.2 the aforesaid O.C. suit No. 35 of 1969 was instituted impleading defendant No. 2 and the plaintiff obtained an ex-parte decree which was sought to be set aside by the Government respondent by filing O.C. Suit No. 102 of 1973. After obtaining the ex-parte decree the plaintiff of O.C. Suit No. 35 of 1969 started other Execution Case No.22 of 1969 and obtained a kabala executed Through Court on 31.7.72 and also got his name mutated in the record of right and on payment of rent got dakilas and also realised rents from the tenants of the suit property.

4. Defendant Nos. 3 and 4 tenants of the suit property also filed a separate written statement stating that Lala Ram was the owner in possession of the property in suit and he married Sarna Kumari. Lala Ram permitted Sarna Kumri to adopt a son and Gour Sankar was the adopted son under a deed of adoption, Ext.A(1) executed on 29.7.46. Thus Gour sankar became sole owner of the suit property. Gour sankar migrated to India. But Sarna Kumari was living in Mymensingh and maintained her-self out of the income of the suit properties. Further case of the defendants was that the suit property vested in the Custodian as enemy property and / or abandoned property and Sarna Romani had no authority to enter into a Contract for sale of the suit property with defendant No. 1 and the bainapatra was a fraudulent document and the decree passed in O. C. Suit No.35 of 1969 for specific performance contract was a forged and fraudulent one. Their further case was that they were in possession in a part of the property in suit for more than 12 years and acquired title by adverse possession.

5. The trial Court by its judgment and decree dated 31.3.1980 dismissed the suit with  the findings that the suit property was the exclusive property of Sarna Kumari, that she entered into agreement for sale of the property with defendant No.1 and that defendant No.2 was the son of Sarna Kumari's mother's sister and he was her heir and that she did not adopt Gour Sankar and that the impugned decree passed in O.C. Suit No.35 of 1969 was legal and defendant No.1 acquired legal tide to the property in suit and that he was in possession.

6. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court the plaintiff government preferred F.A. No. 22 of 1991. Defendant No.1 appellant contested the appeal in the High Court Division.

7. The learned Judges of the High Court Division allowed the appeal and reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court on the findings that the suit property belonged to Gour Sankar Roy, the adopted son of Sarna Kumari and Sarna Kumari had no title to and possession in the suit property and that defendant No. 2 had no ownership in the property in suit and no right to transfer the same to defendant No.1 the learned Judges also found that Gour Sankar migrated to India and became citizen of India and that the property vested in the custodian and that without no pleading Gour Sankar Roy or the custodian of the enemy property in the suit the suit was bad for defect of parties and that the ex-parte decree and the kabala are null and void. The Teamed Judges revived O.C. Suit No. 35 of 1969 with the direction to implead Lala Gour Sankar Roy or his heirs, if he is not alive and the Government of Bangladesh as defendants.

8. Mr. S. R. Pal learned Advocate for the appellant contends that none of the courts below having found that the property left by 1 Lola Ram Sankar Roy escheated to the 1 Government and the Government not being a party to O.C. Suit No. 35 of 1969 the learned Judges of the High Court Division fell into an I error of law in not holding that the property in I suit belonged to Sarna Kumari who executed the agreement for sale with defendant no.1 and in that view of the legal position the learned Judges of the High Court Division seriously fell in an error of law in allowing the appeal and reviving O.C. Suit No. 35 of 1969 setting aside ex-parte decree and declaring the kabala executed on the basis of the said ex-parte decree void. He also submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division were also wrong in directing defendant No.1 to implead Lala Gour Sankar Roy or his heirs, as the case may be and the plaintiff Government as defendants in that suit upon an erroneous view that the property in suit was a vested property which was not the case of the plaintiff Government in O.C. Suit No. 102 of 1973 and the learned Judges of the High Court Division made out a third case upon an erroneous view that the property in suit is a vested one.

<u>9. On reference to the averments made in the plaint in O.C. Suit No.102 of 1973 we are unable to found that the plaintiff-respondent have stated that the property in suit is a vested one. From the averments made in this plaint we also find that defendant No.2 in collusion with defendant No. 1 entered into a bainapatra on 17.12.63 showing defendant No. 2 an heir of Sarna Kumari and obtained a decree in O.C. Suit No. 35 of 1969 and pursuant to which defendant No.1 got the kabala executed and registered through the Court. The learned subordinate Judge also found that Pala Ram Sankar and Gour Sankar had no right, tide , interest and possession in the suit property and Sarna Kumari had absolute right, title interest and possession in the suit property and she entered into an agreement with defendant No.1 for sale of the suit property on 17.12.1963 and delivered possession of the suit property to defendant No.1 but before execution and registration of the kabala she died childless leaving Benode Lal Roy, her mother's sister's son, as her only heir. Neither from the averments made in the plaint we find that the plaintiff claimed the property in suit as a vested property nor we find that the learned Subordinate Judge held that the property is a vested property. But inspite of such averments made in the plaint and the finding of the learned Subordinate Judge the learned Judges of the High Court Division have made out a third case in holding that the property is a vested property. Mr. Pal rightly contended that the learned Judges of the High Court Division made out a third case in holding that the property in suit is a vested property. For the above reasons we are of the opinion that the teamed Judges of the High Court Division wrongly held that the suit property is a vested Property.</u>

10. Being confronted with these contentions Mr. Fazlul Karim the learned Advocate for respondent Nos. 3(1) and 4(2) felt difficulty to repel the contentions of Mr. pal. Mr. Shahidul Islam Chowdhury., teamed Advocate for respondent No.1, also felt similar difficulty.

11. Accordingly, we allow the appeal and set aside the impugned Judgment and decree dated 16.7.91 of the High Court Division without any order as to costs and restore those of the trial court.

End.
